assets.title: Короткий задний козырёк
assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Primary request: Reinterpret the supplied hand-painted fantasy prop concepts as exactly ONE wooden merchant counter stall with a cloth canopy, shelves and merchandise on multiple levels. Transfer the actual visual rendering language of these concepts precisely.
Input images: Image 1 (smithy) is the main STYLE AND CONSTRUCTION anchor; Images 2 (crate), 3 (bucket), 4 (anvil), and 5 (weapon rack) are supporting STYLE references for chunky proportions, hand-painted faceted wood, plain metal and simplified materials. They are NOT objects to include. Preserve their stylization while replacing their subjects with the merchant stall described below. Ignore all flags, insignia, light sources, glowing liquids, forge, stone chimney, weapons and magic in the references.
STYLE IS CRITICAL: a painted stylized fantasy game prop with bold chunky BEVELED geometry, deliberately carved uneven timber, broad visible brush strokes, broad warm ochre/golden-brown wood colour planes, a small number of thick painted wood-grain strokes, large polygonal facets on corners and ends, dark simple iron bands and oversized round rivets. Like the supplied crate, bucket and smithy, every board is a few strong painted planes. Canvas has only a few large angular planar folds and clear flat colour masses. Keep a clean volumetric silhouette and strong readable shapes, not a realistic product render. NO photorealism, NO PBR-looking materials, NO photographic fibre texture, NO fine woven cloth, NO tiny wood pores, NO microtexture, NO dense scratch noise, NO smooth realistic fabric simulation. Do not use any of the previously generated merchant images as style.
Palette: rich warm ochre and honey-brown painted timber as in the references, plain dark desaturated iron, faded olive-green canvas, oatmeal cloth parcels, muted brown leather, simple earthy terracotta pottery. Large coherent colour blocks. Canvas is plain, no printed or embroidered design.
GAMEPLAY READABILITY IS CRITICAL: render from the ACTUAL high gameplay camera, orthographic projection looking downward at 48 degrees below horizontal with approximately 35 degrees azimuth for a front three-quarter view. Do not lower the camera to reveal hidden goods. Design the architecture itself to reveal the goods from this high viewpoint. Put the shallow canopy on the FAR side relative to the camera, over only a small rear or far-side section. Its projected silhouette must NOT cover the front countertop, stepped displays or merchandise. At least 75 percent of the display area is clearly exposed from above. No front posts, hanging valance, or transverse front beam across the open display. Roof occupies at most one quarter of the total footprint. This is a mostly open merchant counter with a SMALL functional fabric canopy behind the merchandise, not a roof covering the entire stall.
Subject: broad sturdy wooden counter body with visible big timber construction and open shelves. Merchandise grouped into 4 to 6 large distinct readable units at three heights: a low side crate, the exposed main counter, and a short raised shelf in front of or beside the canopy. Goods are plain chunky wooden crates, one or two large rolled cloth bundles, tied coarse parcels and simple pottery; no tiny clutter. Clear physical separation of body, canopy frame, fabric and merchandise groups, believable contact and construction, open trader standing space, all parts assembled. Fit roughly a 5.2 by 3.8 metre footprint; canopy height around 2.7 metres, no dimension labels.
Composition: exactly ONE complete assembled stall per image. No sheet, collage, panels, extra view, exploded drawing, or duplicated stall. Show the entire object and every foot with a comfortable transparent margin. It fills most of the square image. The open display and goods are the focal point; the roof is visually secondary.
Presentation: neutral even albedo-like colour visibility with only simplified painted form shading matching the references. No directional sunlight, sunset tint, theatrical lighting, reflected orange light, hard lighting shadows or cast shadow under the asset. No luminous highlights or glow. Painted broad bevel colour accents are allowed; no photographic specular highlights.
Background: genuine transparent alpha, including open spaces and gaps. No black/white/coloured opaque backdrop, no checkerboard, no ground, platform, rug, vegetation, horizon, environment or contact shadow.
Hard exclusions: flags, banners, pennants, heraldry, coats of arms, crests, emblems, symbols, runes, signs, text, watermark, logos, people, animals, lanterns, lamps, candles, torches, flames, sparks, smoke, glowing contents, weapons, shields, smithing equipment. Do not copy unwanted features from the style references.

VARIANT CONSTRUCTION: a straight wide counter with a narrow raised rear shelf. Two thick timber posts on the far rear edge support a very SHALLOW single-slope olive cloth canopy behind the raised shelf. The fabric strip is about one fifth of the total stall depth, taut with three broad angular painted folds, and its front edge ends BEHIND the merchandise row. The entire main counter is uncovered open air. Attach a low crate ledge at one end and a higher compact goods display at the other. No tall front uprights or front overhang. Strong simple rectangular silhouette.
